images.title: Take the smaller count
images.purpose: Show the HCF of 30 and 72 built by taking each common prime the minimum number of times it occurs.
images.composition: One small count table sits in the centre with large digits; a single result line sits below it, with wide white margins.
exact_structure: Top line above the table: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 and 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.
Table with exactly 3 rows and 3 columns plus a header row; header cells: blank, How many 2s, How many 3s.
Row Minimum: 1 | 1, with both cells shaded light reddish purple #CC79A7.
Result line below the table: HCF = 2 × 3 = 6.
rejection: any count cell that does not match the factorisations (30 has one 2 and one 3; 72 has three 2s and two 3s)
a column for the prime 5, which is not common
images.takeaway: For each common prime, take the smaller count, then multiply.
images.description: A table counting 2s and 3s in 30 and 72, with a minimum row of 1 and 1, giving HCF = 2 × 3 = 6.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on taking the minimum count of each common prime.
images.teaching_notes: Read each column and circle the smaller number; that is how many times the prime goes into the HCF.

image_decisions.why: A small count table makes the minimum count rule concrete.
